title: Computational complexity: a linear scan

source_policy: Definition-level references support the mathematical vocabulary. Stories and worked quantities are originally authored constructed examples, not measurements or historical events. Historical priority and notation claims require separate evidence before publication.
purpose: Count a full scan and separate input size, cost per operation and modeled runtime.
meaning: Computational complexity studies the resources required by algorithms as input size grows. This introductory specimen derives a linear operation count from a specified full scan, then assigns a constant cost per inspection. It keeps asymptotic growth, exact counts and modeled elapsed time separate.

definition.setting: Algorithm analysis with one declared basic operation: inspect each item once in a full scan. The display contains a bounded number of items, while the stated scan rule defines the general positive-integer family.
definition.formal_latex: w(n)=n,\quad T(n)=c n,\quad T(2n)=2c n,\quad w(n)\in O(n).

signature.n,itemCount: Positive integer number of items in [1,32].
signature.c,costPerItem: Fixed stipulated per-item cost in [0,10] milliseconds.
signature.w(n),operationCount: Exactly n inspections for the specified full scan.
signature.T(n),totalTime: Primary modeled time c*n in milliseconds.
signature.2n,doubledCount: Twice the item count, retained as a separate comparison.
signature.T(2n),doubledTime: Modeled time for twice the input at the same per-item cost.
signature.O(n): An asymptotic upper-bound class, not a measured number.

conditions: The specified full-scan procedure visits every one of n items exactly once, for each positive integer input size n. One item inspection is the chosen basic operation.
The executable itemCount is an integer from 1 to 32. The conceptual operation-count family w(n)=n is defined for every positive integer n; the finite drawing is only a bounded demonstration.
A fixed stipulated cost c in [0,10] milliseconds per item gives model time T(n)=c*n. Setup, loop-control, memory, parallelism and changing per-item costs are outside this cost model.
For the doubled input the same fixed c gives 2n inspections and T(2n)=c*(2n)=2*T(n). A full scan does not stop early on a matching item.
The operation count w(n)=n has tight linear growth Θ(n), hence also the upper-bound class O(n). These are asymptotic classes, not numeric runtimes.

For each fixed c>0, the model time c*n also has tight linear growth. When c=0 the idealized model time is zero while the number of inspections is still n; zero time does not have a positive linear lower bound.
A formula derived from the specified procedure supports the growth statement. Observing a finite graph or a measured doubling ratio alone does not prove an asymptotic claim.
Milliseconds here are stipulated costs, not measured benchmarks or performance promises for a real device.
Under the stated fixed positive cost per inspection, this full scan is a linear-time algorithm; a zero modeled cost does not change its inspection count.
definition.domain_notes: The broader field includes many time and space models, worst-case and average-case questions, and classes of computational problems. This card analyzes only a full scan under a constant per-item cost assumption. It does not run a benchmark, analyze arbitrary code, compare machines, estimate hidden overhead, or infer O(n) from a short plot. The synthetic c=0 boundary remains valid arithmetic but is not a physical timing claim.
definition.proof_status: Definition-level references; restricted-family properties are author-derived. Independent mathematical review pending.

grammar.expression_latex: w(n)=n,\quad T(n)=c n,\quad T(2n)=2c n,\quad w(n)\in O(n).
grammar.formation_rule: operationCount=itemCount; doubledCount=2*itemCount; output=totalTime=costPerItem*operationCount; doubledTime=costPerItem*doubledCount. For this full-scan family, w(n)∈Θ(n); T(n)∈Θ(n) when c>0.
grammar.precedence: Count the explicitly chosen item inspections first, then multiply by their fixed per-item time. Doubling n is distinct from doubling c, although either doubles this particular product.

properties.claim: The specified full scan performs exactly n selected basic inspections.

properties.derivation: Associate each distinct item with one and only one inspection. This gives w(n)=n for every positive integer n in the family.

properties.claim: Doubling input size doubles modeled time at fixed c.
properties.conditions: Keep the per-item cost constant and use the same full scan.
properties.derivation: T(2n)=c*(2n)=2*(c*n)=2*T(n), including the synthetic c=0 case.
properties.status: author-derived for stated conditions; independent review pending

properties.claim: Changing c does not change the operation-count growth.
properties.conditions: Keep the inspection procedure fixed; use a finite nonnegative constant c for each run.
properties.derivation: w(n)=n remains a tight linear count. For c>0, T(n)=cn is also Θ(n); at c=0 only the modeled time is zero.

prompts.prompt: Why not call a matching-item search the same full scan?
prompts.answer: A search may stop before visiting all items. Its best, worst and average cases can differ; this declared procedure deliberately inspects every item.

prompts.prompt: Does zero assigned inspection time mean zero operations?
prompts.answer: No. The synthetic boundary c=0 makes T(n)=0 in the arithmetic model, while w(n)=n still counts all inspections.

representations.description: Numbered work tiles, distinct n and 2n inspection counts and modeled time bars connect the cost model to actual chosen basic operations.
T(n) and T(2n) are plotted against continuous cost per item c at fixed integer n. The comparison changes the stipulated constant, not the algorithm or input count.
The input size, chosen operation count, per-operation time and total modeled time retain distinct quantities and units.
